correctness.rationale: Both extreme recurrence coefficients of F^t are 1, giving bilateral surjectivity and a t-dimensional homogeneous space K_t with t consecutive free coordinates. Kernel trace surjectivity suffices for full image. It is also necessary for each fixed pattern: evaluating arbitrary configurations on the pinned sites exhausts the trace space, and a proper kernel trace gives a proper, varying coset as the target varies. At time b=2^m Frobenius makes K_b exactly the b-periodic sequences, so fullness is residue injectivity; fullness persists because F is onto. This includes a singleton at time one and m=0. Counting one site per occupied residue gives the binomial quotient; the log of the falling-factorial ratio is −k(k−1)/(2b)+O(k³/b²+k²/N) in the stated scaling, proving the phase-dependent limit. For the unrounded clock, z^s maps to evaluation on K_t, relations include (1+z)^t, and the t consecutive independent evaluations prove that the induced Laurent quotient is the full dual. Hence the first full-image time is one plus the maximum root order of a nonempty subset sum. For triples, odd subsets have order zero, and a pair has order 2^v₂(gap), by Frobenius and the simple root of the odd-power binomial, valid also after translating negative indices. Therefore the triple CDF at 1+2^(m−1) is exactly the injective-residue CDF with k=3. In the telescoping moments the tail numerator is 3·2^(−m)−2·4^(−m)−3/N+2/N² over Δ_N. Summing with increments 2^(m−1) and 3·4^(m−1), respectively, gives (5) and (6); the squared mean is O(R²) and the second moment has leading term 3N/2. The limiting CDFs at 3 and 5 are 3/8 and 21/32. These are statements about uniform unordered samples without replacement, the general rounded clock and the specifically three-site unrounded clock.
